analysis.title: Chip rout tests AI investment case (UBS House View - Daily Asia)
key_insights: US tech led markets lower on Thursday 5 Nov 2026 as the post-election relief rally reversed. The Nasdaq 100 fell about 6.4% and the S&P 500 about 4.4%.
The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index fell 12.3%, extending its drawdown since June to about 38.3%. Qualcomm fell sharply after its profit outlook disappointed.

Investors are reassessing how Democratic gains, especially at the state level, affect AI infrastructure and data centers. The focus is electricity use, water use, permitting and development costs, and greater congressional oversight.

UBS says the decline reflects uncertainty about the cost and pace of the data center buildout, not a sudden deterioration in the outlook. The sharp divergence across equity sectors suggests the move was not driven mainly by macro concerns.

Investors are shifting from rewarding spending commitments to demanding evidence of monetization, capacity utilization, returns and the ability to raise capital. High expectations and concentrated positions raise the sensitivity of AI stocks to guidance, regulation and risk appetite.

UBS expects broad federal restrictions on data centers to face legislative and presidential constraints unless a widespread AI security issue occurs. State and local decisions are more likely to set where projects are built, their cost and their speed.

Proposed US data center capacity of about 400 GW far exceeds UBS's buildout assumption of about 90 GW by 2030. UBS says regulation may redistribute and extend the investment cycle rather than derail it, with power access, permitting, financing and execution separating winners from losers.

UBS cites accelerating cloud revenue, growing advance orders for computing capacity and significant chip backlogs among Chinese buyers. It forecasts AI capital spending of USD 1.0tr in 2026, USD 1.4tr in 2027 and USD 1.5tr in 2028.

UBS sees upside in broad equity indices over 6-12 months and calls the sell-off overdone. It would use the volatility to add diversified exposure to higher-quality companies, and acknowledges investors may need more clarity on data center policy before volatility abates.
UBS advises reducing excessive single-stock concentration relative to tech and broad benchmarks, since volatility has been higher at the single-stock level than in the indices.

UBS cut its US IT sector preference to Neutral in February. Its preferred equity sectors are industrials, health care and financials. Regionally it prefers the Eurozone, emerging markets and Asia ex-Japan. Investors overweight US tech versus benchmark should consider rebalancing.

UBS suggests investors with large bond underweights rebuild strategic allocations, favoring high-quality short- to medium-maturity bonds and emerging market bonds. Alternatives and commodities add other return drivers.

Germany's fiscal expansion is showing up in defense, construction and labor demand. The federal deficit widened to EUR 64.2bn in the quarter to September, about two-thirds of the annual target. Federal investment spending slowed in Q3.

UBS forecasts German GDP growth rising from 1.0% in 2026 to 1.5% in 2027. It stays constructive on German equities, expects little Bund yield impact from higher issuance, and favors quality European government and corporate bonds.
Market moves on the day: Brent rebounded to about USD 99 per barrel, the US 10-year yield fell 5bp to 4.84%, and gold rose 0.7%.

trade_ideas.description: Use volatility to add diversified exposure to higher-quality companies across AI platforms, applications and infrastructure (foundry, compute, power)
trade_ideas.rationale: The sell-off looks overdone given UBS's base case of only modest changes to the pace, timing and cost of data center deployment.
trade_ideas.risk: Investors may need more certainty about the data center policy environment before volatility abates.

trade_ideas.description: Rebalance excess US technology exposure toward industrials, health care and financials

trade_ideas.description: Rebuild strategic bond allocations in high-quality short- to medium-maturity bonds and emerging market bonds
trade_ideas.rationale: UBS sees diversification and income potential in fixed income as a hedge against further equity volatility.

risk_factors: Greater congressional oversight and state-level changes could raise the cost and delay data center projects through electricity, water, permitting and development costs.
AI-linked stocks are sensitive to guidance, regulation and risk appetite because of high expectations and concentrated positions.
Signs that AI revenue growth is slowing, cloud utilization is weakening, or lower AI costs fail to generate enough new usage would signal a lasting downturn.

Algorithmic efficiency gains that sharply cut compute needs, larger investments that fail to deliver commensurate AI capability gains, or tighter financial conditions that constrain big tech spending would lead UBS to reassess.
A widespread AI security issue could bring broad federal restrictions.
Germany: implementation bottlenecks, capacity constraints, skills mismatches and supply-chain bottlenecks could slow fiscal pass-through.
vol_and_positioning: Volatility has been higher at the individual stock level than in the broad indices.
High expectations and concentrated positions have made AI-linked stocks more sensitive to guidance, regulation and risk appetite.
The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index is down about 38.3% from its June high after a 12.3% one-day drop.
geopolitical: Oil and geopolitical developments were a secondary source of volatility, with Brent rebounding to about USD 99.
US midterm results: Democratic gains, especially at the state level, and the prospect of congressional gridlock and greater oversight of AI infrastructure and data centers.

tension_points.bull_case: Demand remains strong: cloud revenue is accelerating, advance orders for compute are growing and proposed capacity of about 400 GW far exceeds UBS's 90 GW assumption. UBS forecasts AI capex rising to USD 1.5tr by 2028.
tension_points.bear_case: Investors are demanding evidence of monetization, utilization, returns and ability to raise capital. State-level opposition and congressional oversight could raise data center costs and delay projects, and concentrated positions amplify the downside.
tension_points.what_invalidates: AI-related revenue growth slowing, cloud utilization weakening, or lower AI costs failing to generate enough new usage to absorb expanding capacity.
